subject.title: [Google Antigravity Ban] Frequent Tool Schema Reloading Causes False Positive Anti-Abuse Detection

question: Should OpenClaw land a bounded internal cache for provider-normalized tool schema parameters now, or defer this issue to the broader prepared-runtime migration?
rationale: The repeated-normalization path is source-proven, but the permanent cache boundary affects provider hooks, plugin metadata lifecycle, custom provider behavior, and the prepared-runtime direction.

options.title: Land a bounded internal cache
options.body: Refresh the open cache PR or replace it with the same narrow shape: cache cloned schema parameters only for known safe provider hooks and preserve fresh tool objects and closures per turn.

options.title: Defer to prepared runtime
options.body: Keep the issue open until the prepared-runtime rollout carries enough provider/tool facts to remove the repeated work without a separate cache layer.

options.title: Require live proof first
options.body: Hold implementation until a maintainer or reporter captures current-main Google/Gemini or heap proof showing the user-visible impact still occurs.

recommendation.title: Land a bounded internal cache
recommendation.body: Refresh the open cache PR or replace it with the same narrow shape: cache cloned schema parameters only for known safe provider hooks and preserve fresh tool objects and closures per turn.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision is centered on provider-runtime hook behavior and compatibility boundaries, where the source history points to provider family hook work.
